And it has come in the tafsīr: "Allah's remembrance of you when you remember Him is greater than your remembrance [of Him]." Another aspect, whose meaning is: ”وَلَذِكْرُ اللَّهِ أكْبَرُ“ — it, the prohibition of indecency and wrongdoing, is greater than refraining from indecency and wrongdoing, because Allah has forbidden them both.

zajjaj:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿وَلا تُجادِلُوا أهْلَ الكِتابِ إلا بِالَّتِي هي أحْسَنُ﴾ — i.e. the people of war [Translator's note: so in the source, «أهْلَ الحَرْبِ»; the explanation that follows speaks of the people of the jizya, and the intended sense may be "not the people of war"]. So the meaning is: "Do not dispute with the people of the jizya (poll-tax) except in the way that is best, and fight those who have done wrong." And it has been said: the verse is abrogated by His saying: ﴿قاتِلُوا الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ ولا بِاليَوْمِ الآخِرِ ولا يُحَرِّمُونَ ما حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ ورَسُولُهُ ولا يَدِينُونَ دِينَ الحَقِّ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ حَتّى يُعْطُوا الجِزْيَةَ عَنْ يَدٍ وهم صاغِرُونَ﴾ [al-Tawba: 29]; so the state of being humbled (al-ṣaghār) lay outside "اَلَّتِي هي أحْسَنُ" (the way that is best), and therefore it is more likely that it is abrogated. It is also possible that the humbling is the taking of the jizya from them even if they dislike it. Those from whom the jizya is taken — by the explicit text of the Book — are the Jews and the Christians, because they are the people of the Torah and the Gospel. As for the Magians, the jizya was taken from them because of the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: «سُنُّوا بِهِمْ سُنَّةَ أهْلِ الكِتابِ» ("Treat them in the way the People of the Book are treated"). People have differed about the other unbelievers besides these, such as idol-worshippers and those like them. According to Mālik ibn Anas they are treated in the same way: the jizya is taken from them, whether they are non-Arabs or Arabs. As for the people of Iraq, they said: we accept the jizya from non-Arabs who are not Arabs, if they are unbelievers, even if they fall outside these categories — I mean the Jews, the Christians and the Magians — such as the Indians, the Turks and the Daylam. As for the Arabs, in their view, if they fall outside these three categories no jizya is accepted from them, and killing was the ruling in their case if they persisted in a religion other than Judaism, Christianity and Magianism. And some of the jurists hold nothing but killing for the worshippers of idols and statues and those like them.

zajjaj:48-48.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما كُنْتَ تَتْلُو مِن قَبْلِهِ مِن كِتابٍ ولا تَخُطُّهُ بِيَمِينِكَ إذًا لارْتابَ المُبْطِلُونَ﴾ — i.e. you had not read the scriptures, nor were you one who writes; and such is the description of the Prophet ﷺ with them in the Torah and the Gospel.
His saying: ﴿إذًا لارْتابَ المُبْطِلُونَ﴾ — it has been said: they are the unbelievers of Quraysh.

zajjaj:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿بَلْ هو آياتٌ بَيِّناتٌ في صُدُورِ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا العِلْمَ﴾ — it has been said that there are three aspects in it. Among them: "Rather, the Qur'an is clear signs." Among them: "Rather, the Prophet ﷺ and his affairs are clear signs." And among them: ”بَلْ هو آياتٌ بَيِّناتٌ“, i.e. rather, [the fact] that he neither reads nor writes is clear signs; because if he had not read a book, nor was he one who writes, and then he told the stories of the ancients and of the prophets, then that is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge.

zajjaj:51-51.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَكْفِهِمْ أنّا أنْـزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ الكِتابَ يُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ — «Some people among the Muslims had written something down from the Jews, and they brought it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he, upon him be peace, said: "It is enough as foolishness of a people — or the misguidance of a people — that they turn away from what their prophet brought to what someone other than their prophet brought to a people other than theirs."»

zajjaj:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالعَذابِ ولَوْلا أجَلٌ مُسَمًّى لَجاءَهُمُ العَذابُ﴾ — this was revealed about an ignorant people who said: ﴿اللَّهُمَّ إنْ كانَ هَذا هو الحَقَّ مِن عِنْدِكَ فَأمْطِرْ عَلَيْنا حِجارَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 32]. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that there is a set term for their punishment, and He said: ﴿بَلِ السّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهم والسّاعَةُ أدْهى وأمَرُّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 46].
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَيَأْتِيَنَّهم بَغْتَةً﴾ — its meaning is: suddenly (fujāʾatan). ”بَغْتَةً“ is an accusative (manṣūb) noun in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and its meaning is: "and it will surely come upon them taking them by surprise (mufājaʾatan)."

zajjaj:56-56.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إنَّ أرْضِي واسِعَةٌ فَإيّايَ فاعْبُدُونِ﴾ — its interpretation: it has been said that they were commanded to emigrate from the place in which they could not worship Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and fulfil His obligations. The origin of this concerns those who were able [to emigrate] among those who believed and could not make their faith manifest. And likewise it is obligatory upon everyone who is in a land in which disobedience is practised, and who cannot do otherwise, to emigrate and move to where it is possible for him to worship Allah as He truly deserves to be worshipped.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإيّايَ فاعْبُدُونِ﴾ — ”إيّايَ“ is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied verb, which the one that appears explains. The meaning is: "So worship Me — so worship Me" (”فاعْبُدُوا إيّايَ فاعْبُدُونِي“); so one of the two verbs — I mean the second — dispensed with making the first overt. If you say ”فَإيّايَ فاعْبُدُوا“, then ”إيّايَ“ is accusative by what comes after the fā', and you do not make it accusative by an implied verb, just as when you say ”بِزَيْدٍ فامْرُرْ“ (by Zayd, pass), the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to ”اُمْرُرْ“. The meaning is: "My earth is spacious, so worship Me." As for the fā' when you say ”زَيْدًا فاضْرِبْ“ (Zayd, strike), it can only be an apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a condition, as if someone said: "I do not strike ʿAmr, but I strike Zayd," and you said in answer to him: "Then strike Zayd," and then you said: ”زَيْدًا فاضْرِبْ“, making the fronting of the noun a substitute for the condition, as if you had said: "If the matter is as you describe, then strike Zayd." And this is the position of all the Basran grammarians.

zajjaj:58-58.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهم مِنَ الجَنَّةِ غُرَفًا﴾ — and it has been read ”لَنُثَوِّيَنَّهم“, with thāʾ. One says ”ثَوى الرَّجُلُ“ (the man dwelt) when he stays in a place, and ”أثْوَيْتُهُ“ (I lodged him): I settled him in a dwelling in which he stays.

zajjaj:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَأيِّنْ مِن دابَّةٍ لا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَها﴾ — every living creature on the earth, of what has reason and what has no reason, is a dābba (creature); it is simply from ”دَبَّتْ عَلى الأرْضِ، فَهي دابَّةٌ“ (it crept on the earth, so it is a creeper). The meaning is: "a creeping soul (nafs dābba)." And the meaning of ”وَكَأيِّنْ“ is: "and how many a creature (وَكَمْ مِن دابَّةٍ)."
His saying: ﴿لا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَها﴾ — i.e. it does not store up its provision; it simply wakes in the morning and Allah provides for it. Most animals and creeping things are like this, and among the animals that creep there is none that stores up, as far as has become clear, except the ant, for its storing is evident.

zajjaj:64-64.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنَّ الدّارَ الآخِرَةَ لَهي الحَيَوانُ لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — its meaning: it is the abode of everlasting life.

zajjaj:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿فَإذا رَكِبُوا في الفُلْكِ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾ — i.e. they did not pray that their idols, and what they worship alongside Allah, would save them; ﴿فَلَمّا نَجّاهم إلى البَرِّ إذا هم يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ — i.e. they worship others alongside Allah.

zajjaj:66-66.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾ — it has been read with kasra on the lām and with sukūn on it, and the kasra is better, in the sense of: "so that they disbelieve, and so that they enjoy themselves."

zajjaj:69-69.t:
His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا فِينا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهم سُبُلَنا﴾ — Allah made known that He increases those who strive in guidance; just as He leads the transgressors astray and increases the unbelievers in misguidance through their unbelief, so He increases those who strive in guidance. Thus He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿والَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا زادَهم هُدًى وآتاهم تَقْواهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 17]; the meaning is that He gave them the reward of their piety and increased them in guidance upon their guidance.
His saying: ﴿وَإنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ المُحْسِنِينَ﴾ — its interpretation: Allah is their helper, because His saying ﴿والَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا فِينا﴾ — Allah being with them — indicates His helping them; and help consists in their rising above their enemy by prevailing through proof, and prevailing through force and power.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt
Meccan
﷽
His saying: ﴿الم﴾ ﴿أحَسِبَ النّاسُ﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 2]: "الـم" — its interpretation is: "I am Allah, I know best (أنا اللَّهُ أعْلَمُ)". We have explained everything that has been said about this at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.

zajjaj:2-2.t: And His saying: ﴿أحَسِبَ النّاسُ أنْ يُتْرَكُوا أنْ يَقُولُوا آمَنّا﴾: the wording is the wording of an inquiry, and the meaning is the meaning of affirmation and rebuke (taqrīr wa-tawbīkh). Its meaning is: "Did they think that We would be satisfied from them with their saying 'we are believers', only, and that they would not be tested with what makes clear the reality of their faith?" It has come in the exegesis concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَهم لا يُفْتَنُونَ﴾: "they will not be tested with that by which the truthfulness of their faith is known from its falsity"; and it was said: "لا يُفْتَنُونَ" means: they will not be tried in their persons and their wealth, so that through patience under trial the one true in faith is known from others. The position of the first "أنْ" is accusative, [standing for] the ism (noun) of "حَسِبَ" and its khabar (predicate). The position of the second "أنْ" is accusative from two angles. The better of them is that it be accusative through "يُتْرَكُوا", so the meaning is: "Did people think that they would be left for saying (لِأنْ يَقُولُوا)" or "because of saying (بِأنْ يَقُولُوا)"; when the genitive particle was dropped, "يُتْرَكُوا" reached "أنْ" and put it in the accusative (accusative by removal of the preposition). It is also possible that what governs the second is "أحَسِبَ"; as though the meaning on this view — and Allah knows best — were: "Did people think that they would say 'we believe' and not be tested?" The first is better.

zajjaj:3-3.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ فَتَنّا الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾, i.e. We tested and tried.
And His saying: ﴿فَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا ولَيَعْلَمَنَّ الكاذِبِينَ﴾: the meaning is: "He will surely know the truthfulness of the truthful through his truthfulness actually occurring from him, and the lying of the liar through his lying actually occurring from him; and that is what is recompensed." Allah knew the truthful from the liar before He created them both; but the intent is the knowledge's coming to pass of that which is recompensed.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying: ﴿أمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئاتِ أنْ يَسْبِقُونا﴾, i.e. they think that they will escape Us, i.e. they cannot frustrate Us. ﴿ساءَ ما يَحْكُمُونَ﴾, with the meaning "evil is it as a judgement that they judge (ساءَ حُكْمًا يَحْكُمُونَ)", just as you say: "an excellent man is Zayd (نِعْمَ رَجُلًا زَيْدٌ)". It is also possible that it [ما] is nominative, with the meaning: "evil is the judgement, their judgement (ساءَ الحُكْمُ حُكْمُهم)".

zajjaj:5-5.t:
And His saying: ﴿مَن كانَ يَرْجُو لِقاءَ اللَّهِ﴾: its meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "whoever hopes for the reward of meeting Allah". As for whoever said that its meaning is fear: fear is the opposite of hope, and there is no [word with] opposite [meanings] in the speech; we have explained that in the Book of Opposites (Kitāb al-Aḍdād).
And His saying: ﴿فَإنَّ أجَلَ اللَّهِ لآتٍ﴾: "مَن" is in the sense of a condition; it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is "كانَ", and the apodosis (jawāb al-jazāʾ) is: ﴿فَإنَّ أجَلَ اللَّهِ لآتٍ﴾.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَوَصَّيْنا الإنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ حُسْنًا﴾: the reading is "حُسْنًا", and "إحْسانًا" has also been transmitted. "حُسْنًا" is better because it agrees with the Muṣḥaf. Whoever says "حُسْنًا", it is like "We enjoined (وَصَّيْنا)" [him] to do toward his parents what is good. Whoever reads "إحْسانًا", its meaning is: "We enjoined man to do good to his parents, a doing of good (أنْ يُحْسِنَ إلى والِدَيْهِ إحْسانًا)". It seems that "حُسْنًا" is more general in [the sense of] dutifulness. [Translator's note: the source has إلّا أنْ يَفْعَلَ ("except that he do"), apparently for إلى أنْ / أنْ يَفْعَلَ; translated according to the evident sense.]
And His saying: ﴿وَإنْ جاهَداكَ لِتُشْرِكَ بِي ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ فَلا تُطِعْهُما﴾ means: "And if your parents strive with you, O man, to make you associate with Me", and likewise "عَلى أنْ تُشْرِكَ بِي". It is narrated that a man left Mecca emigrating to the Prophet ﷺ in Medina, and his mother swore that no roof would shade her until he returned. So Allah made known that dutifulness to parents is obligatory, and forbade that they be followed in disobedience to Allah and in associating partners with Him, even if that is dutifulness in the parents' view.

zajjaj:10-10.t: And His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ النّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ آمَنّا بِاللَّهِ فَإذا أُوذِيَ في اللَّهِ جَعَلَ فِتْنَةَ النّاسِ كَعَذابِ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. when harm or torment befalls him because of his faith, he is as distressed by that as one is distressed by the punishment of Allah. The believer ought to bear harm patiently for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّبِعُوا سَبِيلَنا ولْنَحْمِلْ خَطاياكُمْ﴾: "وَلِنَحْمِلْ" is read with a sukūn on the lām and with a kasra on it, in His saying "وَلْنَحْمِلْ". It is a command in the sense of condition and response (al-sharṭ wa-l-jazāʾ); the meaning is: "If you follow our way, we will bear your sins."
And the meaning is: "If there is any sin in it, we will bear it." The meaning of "سَبِيلَنا" is: the road in our religion which we travel. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that they will not bear anything of their sins, and said: ﴿وَما هم بِحامِلِينَ مِن خَطاياهم مِن شَيْءٍ﴾; its meaning is: "anything that would lighten the punishment for the one whose burden is borne". Then He made known that they will bear their own burdens and burdens along with their burdens, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿لِيَحْمِلُوا أوْزارَهم كامِلَةً يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ ومِن أوْزارِ الَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهم بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 25]; and He said in this sūra: ﴿وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أثْقالَهم وأثْقالا مَعَ أثْقالِهِمْ﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 13]. The explanation of this has come in the ḥadīth: «Whoever establishes a practice of wrongdoing — or: whoever establishes an evil practice — upon him is its sin and the sin of whoever acts on it, without anything being diminished from the burdens of those who act on it; and whoever establishes a good practice has its reward and the reward of whoever acts on it until the Day of Resurrection, without anything being diminished from their rewards.» And [it is] on [the pattern of] His saying: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ ما قَدَّمَتْ وأخَّرَتْ﴾ [al-Infiṭār: 5], i.e. it knows what deeds it sent forward and what practice of good or evil it established, for that is among what it left behind. It is also possible that "ما قَدَّمَتْ وأخَّرَتْ" is: what deeds it sent forward, and what it held back of what it ought to have sent forward. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that He will rebuke them, and said: ﴿وَلَيُسْألُنَّ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ عَمّا كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 13]; that is a questioning of rebuke, as He said: ﴿وَقِفُوهم إنَّهم مَسْؤُولُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 24]. As for a questioning to seek information, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made known that He does not question to seek information, in His saying: ﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يُسْألُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إنْسٌ ولا جانٌّ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 39]

zajjaj:14-14.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ ألْفَ سَنَةٍ إلا خَمْسِينَ عامًا﴾: exception is used in the speech of the Arabs, and its interpretation according to the grammarians is the emphasis of the number, its exact determination and its completeness. For you may mention a total while what actually obtains is most of it; so when you want to emphasise its completeness you say "all of it (كُلُّها)", and when you want to emphasise its deficiency you bring exception into it. You say: "Your brothers came to me (جاءَنِي إخْوَتُكَ)", meaning that all of them came to you, and it is possible that you mean that most of them came to you. When you say: "Your brothers came to me, all of them (جاءَنِي إخْوَتُكَ كُلُّهم)", you have emphasised the sense of the whole group and made known that not one of them stayed behind. You also say: "Your brothers came to me except Zayd (جاءَنِي إخْوَتُكَ إلّا زَيْدًا)", and so you emphasise that the group lacks Zayd. Likewise the round numbers are likened to groups: you say "I have ten (عِنْدِي عَشَرَةٌ)", and it may be short, and it may be complete; when you say "ten less a half (عَشَرَةٌ إلّا نِصْفًا)" or "a full ten (عَشَرَةٌ كامِلَةٌ)", you have made it exact. Likewise when you say "a thousand less fifty (ألْفٌ إلّا خَمْسِينَ)", it is like your saying "ten less a half", because you have used exception only for what belongs more to ten than to nine, since the half has entered within the domain of ten. If you said "ten less one (عَشَرَةٌ إلّا واحِدًا)" or "less two", it would be permissible, but there is ugliness in it, because nine and eight express that number; yet it is permissible by way of emphasising that these nine neither exceed nor fall short, since in your saying "ten less one" you have stated the exact number and excepted what makes a deficiency from the round number. The preferred thing in exception from numbers that are decades (ʿuqūd) is fractions, while it is permissible to except whole numbers. As for excepting half of the thing, it is very ugly; the Arabs do not speak so. When you say "ten less five (عَشَرَةٌ إلّا خَمْسَةً)", ten is not in the vicinity of five, because it is not close to it. You speak with exception just as you speak with diminution: you say "I have a dirham less a qīrāṭ (عِنْدِي دِرْهَمٌ يَنْقُصُ قِيراطًا)"; and if you said "I have a dirham less five dāniqs" or "less half of it", the more fitting for that would be: "I have half a dirham". Exception has only come in the speech of the Arabs as "a little out of a lot". This is a sufficient summary.
And His saying: ﴿فَأخَذَهُمُ الطُّوفانُ وهم ظالِمُونَ﴾: "al-ṭūfān (الطُّوفانُ) of anything" is what is abundant and surrounds the whole group, such as the flood that engulfs great cities; it is called "ṭūfān". Likewise widespread killing and sweeping death are a ṭūfān.

zajjaj:15-15.t: And His saying: ﴿فَأنْجَيْناهُ وأصْحابَ السَّفِينَةِ﴾: He has made clear in another verse who the people of the ship were, in His saying: ﴿قُلْنا احْمِلْ فِيها مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ وأهْلَكَ إلا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ القَوْلُ﴾ [Hūd: 40]

zajjaj:16-16.t: And His saying: ﴿وَإبْراهِيمَ إذْ قالَ لِقَوْمِهِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ واتَّقُوهُ﴾: the meaning is: "And We sent Abraham (وَأرْسَلْنا إبْراهِيمَ)", conjoined to "نُوحًا".

zajjaj:17-17.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّما تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ أوْثانًا وتَخْلُقُونَ إفْكًا﴾, and it has been read: "وَتُخَلِّقُونَ إفْكًا". "أوْثانًا" means: idols. "وَتَخْلُقُونَ إفْكًا" has two views: "you invent lies"; and it was said: you make the idols; and the interpretation on this view would be: "You only worship idols besides Allah, while you yourselves make them."

zajjaj:19-19.t:
And His saying: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَيْفَ يُبْدِئُ اللَّهُ الخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ﴾, and it is also read "تَرَوْا" with tāʾ.
﴿ثُمَّ اللَّهُ يُنْشِئُ النَّشْأةَ الآخِرَةَ﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 20], i.e. then Allah will raise them a second time, by bringing them into being another time, as He said: ﴿وَأنَّ عَلَيْهِ النَّشْأةَ الأُخْرى﴾ [al-Najm: 47]. Most of the reading is "النَّشْأةَ" with a sukūn on the shīn and without lengthening; Abū ʿAmr read: "والنَّشاءَةَ الأُخْرى" with lengthening.

zajjaj:22-22.t: And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَما أنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ في الأرْضِ ولا في السَّماءِ﴾, i.e. no creature in the heaven or on the earth can frustrate Allah. There are two views on this. One of them: its meaning is "you are not able to frustrate [Him] on the earth, nor are the people of heaven able to frustrate [Him] in heaven", i.e. "those in the heavens and those on the earth are unable to frustrate [Him]". It is also possible — and Allah knows best —: "you are not able to frustrate [Him] on the earth, nor even if you were in heaven", i.e. there is no refuge from Allah except in Him.

zajjaj:23-23.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ ولِقائِهِ أُولَئِكَ يَئِسُوا مِن رَحْمَتِي﴾: it is narrated from Qatāda that he said: "Allah condemned a people who were of no account to Him, and said: ﴿أُولَئِكَ يَئِسُوا مِن رَحْمَتِي﴾, and He said: ﴿إنَّهُ لا يَيْأسُ مِن رَوْحِ اللَّهِ إلا القَوْمُ الكافِرُونَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 87]." The believer ought not to despair of Allah's relief, nor of His mercy, nor feel secure from His punishment and penalty; the description of the believer is that he is hopeful of Allah and fearful.

zajjaj:24-24.t:
﴿فَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ إلا أنْ قالُوا اقْتُلُوهُ﴾: al-Ḥasan read "فَما كانَ جَوابُ قَوْمِهِ" in the nominative. Whoever uses the accusative makes "أنْ قالُوا" the ism (noun) of "كانَ"; whoever puts al-jawāb in the nominative makes it the ism of "كانَ" and makes the khabar (predicate) "أنْ قالُوا" and what it governs; and the meaning is: "the answer was nothing but their saying: kill him". When Abraham called them to the oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and argued against them that they worshipped what neither harmed nor benefited them, they made the answer: ﴿اقْتُلُوهُ أوْ حَرِّقُوهُ﴾.
And His saying: ﴿فَأنْجاهُ اللَّهُ مِنَ النّارِ﴾: the meaning is: "So they burned him, and Allah saved him from the fire." It is narrated «that the fire did not affect anything of Abraham ﷺ except the bonds with which he was tied». It is also narrated that all the beasts and vermin were trying to put out [the fire] from Abraham except the gecko, which was blowing on the fire, so its killing was commanded. And it is reported that no benefit was had from fire on that day, I mean the day they seized Abraham, peace be upon him. All that we have mentioned in this story is among what ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal narrated from his father; and likewise most of what I have narrated in this book of exegesis is from the Book of Exegesis from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal.

zajjaj:25-25.t: And He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَقالَ إنَّما اتَّخَذْتُمْ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ أوْثانًا﴾, i.e. Abraham said to his people: you have only taken these idols in order to have affection for one another through them in the life of this world. ﴿ثُمَّ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ يَكْفُرُ بَعْضُكم بِبَعْضٍ ويَلْعَنُ بَعْضُكم بَعْضًا﴾: this is as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿الأخِلاءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بَعْضُهم لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ إلا المُتَّقِينَ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67]. There are four ways of reading in it, among them: "مَوَدَّةَ بَيْنِكم", with fatḥa on "مَوَدَّةَ" and in annexation to "بَيْنِ"; and with "مَوَدَّةً" accusative with tanwīn and "بَيْنَ" accusative: "مَوَدَّةً بَيْنَكم". "مَوَدَّةُ بَيْنِكم" is permissible, nominative and annexed to "بَيْنِ"; and "مَوَدَّةٌ بَيْنَكم" is permissible, nominative with tanwīn and "بَيْنَ" accusative. The accusative in "مَوَدَّةَ" is because it is a mafʿūl lahā (object of purpose), i.e. "you took this for the sake of affection between you". Whoever uses the nominative does so from two angles. One of them is that "ما" be in the sense of "الَّذِي" (relative noun), and the meaning be: "what you have taken as idols besides Allah is the affection between you", so "مَوَدَّةُ" is the khabar (predicate) of "إنَّ". [The other is] that "مَوَدَّةُ" be nominative by implying "it is (هي)", as if He said: "that is an affection between you in the life of this world", i.e. "your intimacy and your gathering around the idols is an affection between you in the life of this world".

zajjaj:26-26.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَآمَنَ لَهُ لُوطٌ وقالَ إنِّي مُهاجِرٌ إلى رَبِّي﴾: Lot believed Abraham, peace be upon him. ﴿وَقالَ إنِّي مُهاجِرٌ إلى رَبِّي﴾: Abraham emigrated from Kūthā to Syria.
And His saying: ﴿وَآتَيْناهُ أجْرَهُ في الدُّنْيا﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 27]: it was said: the good mention [among later generations], and likewise ﴿وَتَرَكْنا عَلَيْهِ في الآخِرِينَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 108]. It was said: "وَآتَيْناهُ أجْرَهُ في الدُّنْيا" means that there is no community among the Muslims, the Jews, the Magians and the Christians but that they revere Abraham. It was said: "وَآتَيْناهُ أجْرَهُ في الدُّنْيا" means that the prophets are from his offspring; and it was said: righteous offspring.

zajjaj:28-28.t: And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلُوطًا إذْ قالَ لِقَوْمِهِ إنَّكم لَتَأْتُونَ الفاحِشَةَ ما سَبَقَكم بِها مِن أحَدٍ مِنَ العالَمِينَ﴾: the meaning is that no male had mounted a male before the people of Lot.

zajjaj:29-29.t: And His saying: ﴿أإنَّكم لَتَأْتُونَ الرِّجالَ﴾: the wording is the wording of a question, and the meaning is the meaning of affirmation and rebuke. ﴿وَتَقْطَعُونَ السَّبِيلَ﴾: it has come in the exegesis: they cut off the way of offspring; and it was said: they waylay people on the roads seeking indecency. ﴿وَتَأْتُونَ في نادِيكُمُ المُنْكَرَ﴾, i.e. you commit evil in your gatherings. It was said that they used to pelt people with pebbles in their gatherings and mock them; so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that this is evil, and that people ought not to keep company on that basis, nor gather except for what brings near to Allah and keeps far from His displeasure, and that they should not gather for mockery and frivolity. And it was said: "وَتَأْتُونَ في نادِيكُمُ المُنْكَرَ" means that they used to act lewdly in their gatherings.
